summary:
The comparison is fair and the protocol is mostly sound. Every method is evaluated from the same cached LightGBM outputs (experiments/evaluate_from_cache3.py build_context): S-NCP and SDLC use the same floored sigma-hat, CQR and S-CQR refit their quantile models for each alpha, and DCP, HPD-split, S-HPD and DLS share SDLC's location-scale density, so those comparisons isolate the calibration rule. BCCP, S-NCP, S-CQR, S-HPD, Mondrian-yhat, DCP and HPD-split are implemented faithfully.

I checked the confirmatory replication in detail:
- **Dataset list.** Through the OpenML API I fetched suites 335 and 336 (36 datasets). Every dataset is accounted for: 17 included, 9 removed for content overlap, 5 duplicate versions, 2 removed by the distinct-value rule, and cpu_act, houses and abalone also removed for overlap.
- **Primary analysis.** I re-ran the frozen pre-registration version of scripts/analyze_confirmatory.py (git archive ccba99b) on results/confirmatory/raw_eval_v3. It reproduces every reported C-H1 to C-H4 statistic exactly: C-H3 geometric-mean ratios 0.862, 0.977, 0.841 and 0.984 with Holm p 0.0011, 0.0077, 0.0006 and 0.0077; C-H2 1 of 17 against a critical value of 3. The only later change in its dependency src/statistics/tests.py is NaN handling, which has no effect here. The primary analysis was therefore run as pre-registered.

Three problems need fixing before submission, and none needs more than minutes of CPU:
1. **Decision study.** The claim that set-based alerts are cheaper when misses are very costly is an artefact of a fixed operating point (recall 0.9 for TC-LS), and the obvious cost-aware rule is missing. My seed-0 computation shows that this rule clearly beats SDLC alerts.
2. **Unreported secondary outcomes.** Pre-registered secondary outcomes are not reported, including an unfavourable one: on the held-out data SDLC-hull is not smaller than S-NCP-hull.
3. **Wording of the pre-registration.** "Pre-registered" and "made public before evaluation" cannot be verified as written. They contradict "will be deposited upon acceptance" and the paper's own definition of pre-registration in Section 5.7, and Supplement S6 prints an internal branch name.

Smaller fixes:
- An overclaiming highlight and an off-by-one method count in the abstract.
- The unqualified BCCP label (a cycle-1 fix that was only partly done).
- A "positive control" that is an arithmetic identity.
- A small fidelity issue in conformal selection.
- Rendering defects in p-value statements.

No essential baseline is missing for the main size and coverage claims.

issues.title: Decision study: operating-point confounding and a missing cost-aware baseline make the alert-cost conclusions unsupported
issues.evidence:
experiments/tail_alerts.py fixes ALPHA = 0.1 for TC-LS and TC-H (recall target 0.9) and compares them with SDLC alerts, whose realised recall is 0.978 (Table 9), at cost ratios r = 10 and 20. The rules are compared at different operating points that do not depend on r. The manuscript's own tests (tables/T13b_alert_tests.md) do not support the conclusion:
- r=20, SDLC vs TC-LS: 22/9, p = 0.083 (r=10: 14/17, p = 0.130).
- At r=20, marginal HPD-split alerts are cheaper than SDLC on 28/31 datasets and S-NCP alerts on 29/31 (both p < 0.001).
- In tables/T14_case_study.md at r=20, the cheapest rules for cps88wages are CQR (0.617), TC-LS (0.626) and SCP (0.633); SDLC costs 0.797 and S-NCP 0.767. For Miami the cheapest is HPD-split (0.075), against SDLC 0.080.
Stratified rules come out cheapest only at r=50 in Fig. 6.
My read-only computation on seed 0 (31 datasets; cached outputs in results/raw_contexts and raw_contexts_v3, scratch script, no files modified) used the plug-in cost-sensitive rule 'alert if P_hat(Y in B_K | x) > 1/(1+r)' from the same location-scale model that TC-LS uses:
- r=10: mean expected cost 0.216 against 0.297 for SDLC; SDLC cheaper on 2/31 datasets.
- r=20: 0.279 against 0.315; SDLC cheaper on 6/31.
The point rule and marginal-set alerts, which also have no guarantee, are already in Table 9, so this rule is an admissible baseline.
The following statements are therefore not supported: Section 6.7 ('set-based alerts with stratum-wise coverage are the cheapest at the highest ratios'), Section 7.2 item 5 ('Set-based alerts ... are cheaper when misses are very costly') and the Conclusion ('set-based alerts are cheaper when missed extremes are very costly').
issues.corrective_action:
Add two rows to Table 9 and Fig. 6: (a) the cost-aware plug-in rule P_hat > 1/(1+r) for each r, and (b) TC-LS with its recall level set per cost ratio, for example alpha_TC in {0.05, 0.02}, or a recall level matched to SDLC's realised recall. Report paired tests against SDLC. Then rewrite:
- Section 6.7, Section 7.2 item 5 and the Conclusion, saying that for yes/no decisions a classifier thresholded for the cost ratio dominates alerts read off sets. The case for sets is the extra information they carry, not the expected cost of alerts.
- The sentence about Fig. 6, which should say that stratified rules are cheapest only at r = 50, and only against fixed-recall rules.
Also state that S-NCP alerts are cheaper than SDLC alerts at every r, including r = 10 (3/27).
issues.new_experiment: Cache-only computation, a few CPU-minutes, no refits. Extend experiments/tail_alerts.py with rules 'Bayes-r' (alert iff sc_t > 1/(1+r), r in {1, 5, 10, 20, 50}) and TC-LS at alpha in {0.05, 0.02}, for 31 datasets x 10 seeds, both sides. Recompute alerts_study in scripts/analyze3.py and Fig. F13 with paired Wilcoxon tests (Holm within each r) of SDLC against each new rule. The locally available raw_contexts holds only seed-0 caches, so this needs the full v2 cache that tail_alerts.py used (or a refit with run_all.py).

issues.title: Pre-registered secondary outcomes of the confirmatory study are not reported, including an unfavourable hull result
issues.evidence:
PREREGISTRATION_confirmatory.md §4 lists as secondary outcomes: upper-tail, top-5% and top-1% coverage, the empty-set rate, worst sigma-hat-decile coverage, the C-H3 comparisons under S10, and the hull variants. §5 promises they will be reported 'whatever their direction'.
- Section 6.5 reports only top-1% coverage, the worst sigma-decile and the price. The supplement has no confirmatory results table: results/confirmatory/tables/C2_main.md and statistics_confirmatory.json 'C-H3_S10_descriptive' are not rendered anywhere.
- From results/confirmatory/raw_eval_v3, using the same per-dataset aggregation and paired_summary as the pre-registered script, SDLC-hull vs S-NCP-hull has a geometric-mean ratio of 1.040 [0.980, 1.144], HL ratio 0.996, 10/7, Wilcoxon p = 0.71. SDLC-hull vs BCCP-hull is 0.893, 13/4, p = 0.007.
- C2_main shows SDLC sets with 2.015 pieces on average, against 1.690 for S-NCP and 1.837 for BCCP.
- Section 7.2 item 4 ('SDLC-hull is valid and remains smaller than BCCP-hull, but it loses part of the advantage') rests on CTR23 only and omits that, on held-out data, SDLC-hull has no advantage over S-NCP-hull.
issues.corrective_action: Add a supplementary table, for example 'Confirmatory replication: secondary outcomes', that renders C2_main (all 17 methods, including SDLC-hull, BCCP-hull and S-NCP-hull) together with the paired hull comparisons and the S10 descriptive comparisons from statistics_confirmatory.json. Add one sentence to Section 6.5: on held-out data, SDLC-hull is smaller than BCCP-hull (0.893, 13/4) but not than S-NCP-hull (1.040, 10/7, p = 0.71), and SDLC sets have more pieces (2.02 vs 1.69). Revise Section 7.2 item 4 so that it recommends S-NCP-hull when an interval is mandatory. Compute the paired hull tests in a separate, clearly labelled script so that the frozen analyze_confirmatory.py stays unchanged.

issues.title: The terms 'pre-registered' and 'made public before evaluation' are unverifiable and inconsistent with the paper's own standard
issues.evidence:
- 01_intro.md and the cover letter say the analysis plan 'was made public before evaluation'. 03_setup.md:60 says it was 'committed it to the public repository'. Yet 07_declarations.md:15 says the code 'will be deposited in a public repository [repository URL] upon acceptance', so a reader cannot verify any 'public' commit.
- Section 5.7 refuses the label 'pre-registered' for the main benchmark because its expectations 'were not registered with a third party'. The confirmatory plan was not registered with a third party either. It sits in the authors' own git history; git timestamps are set by the author.
- Supplement S6 (supplementary_filled.md:510) prints the internal branch name 'claude/amazing-maxwell-i1mihd'.
- The pre-registration commit ccba99b also added partial v3 CTR23 evaluation files (results/raw_eval_v3/44963_*.jsonl, 44964_*.jsonl, ...), so the plan was written after part of the final-implementation CTR23 results existed. This does not invalidate the held-out test but should be disclosed.
- src/statistics/tests.py, which the frozen script imports, changed after ccba99b (Holm NaN handling, n<3 guard). I verified that the ccba99b version of the script reproduces all reported confirmatory statistics exactly, so the change is harmless.
issues.corrective_action:
Before submission, choose one of two routes:
- (a) Make the repository, with its full history, public now and archive it on Software Heritage or Zenodo, so that commit ccba99b and its timestamp can be checked independently. Cite the commit hash and archive DOI in Section 5.7 and S6.
- (b) Replace 'pre-registered' and 'made public before evaluation' throughout (abstract, highlights, intro, Section 5.7, Section 6.5, Table 7 caption, conclusion, cover letter) with 'analysis plan and script fixed and time-stamped in version control (commit ccba99b) before any confirmatory evaluation'.
In either case:
- Remove the branch name from S6.
- Disclose that the plan was committed together with partial CTR23 v3 results.
- Add a sentence stating that a helper module changed after the plan was frozen, and that re-running the frozen version reproduces every number.

issues.title: Headline wording overclaims and the BCCP label is still unqualified (incomplete fix of C1-02 items 1 and 3)
issues.evidence:
- Highlight 4 reads 'SDLC gave the smallest stratum-valid sets on 31 datasets, confirmed on 17'. It was smallest only on average. SDLC beat BCCP on 24/31, S-NCP on 27/31 and S-HPD on 28/31 datasets (Table 5). On the 9 datasets with n < 1600 it was 5/4 against S-NCP (geometric-mean ratio 1.050). On the 15 skewed datasets, Holm p = 0.127 against S-NCP and S-CQR.
- The abstract says SDLC 'was compared with 13 procedures'. MAIN in scripts/analyze3.py:56 (n_methods_main = 13) includes SDLC-LS itself, so SDLC was compared with 12; the intro's 'we compare 13 conformal procedures' is correct.
- Review C1-02 asked for the headline BCCP comparison to be named 'BCCP with the absolute-residual score' and for the text to note that BCCP's reference implementation (pintervals) also offers a heteroscedastic score that is essentially S-NCP. The abstract still says 'smaller than bin-conditional conformal prediction on 24 of 31 datasets'. grep finds no mention of the reference implementation's heteroscedastic option. Against the S-NCP-like variant the gain is only about 2-3% (0.975 CTR23, 0.977 held-out).
issues.corrective_action:
- Highlight 4: 'SDLC gave the smallest stratum-valid sets on average (31 datasets), confirmed on 17 held-out'.
- Abstract: 'compared with 12 other procedures'.
- Abstract: 'smaller than bin-conditional conformal prediction with the absolute-residual score on 24 of 31 datasets'.
- Sections 2.2 and 5.4: one sentence noting that BCCP is score-agnostic and that its reference implementation also offers a scale-normalised residual, which corresponds to S-NCP here, the comparator against which the gain is small.

issues.title: The 'positive control' for target shift is an arithmetic identity, not an empirical check
issues.evidence: evaluate_from_cache3.py shift_weights3 multiplies the importance weight of every test point in the upper stratum by 5 and in the lower stratum by 0.5. The test set is fixed and nothing is recalibrated. Weights that are constant within each stratum leave the within-stratum coverage of any method unchanged by construction. Table 8 shows this for every method: the positive-control worst stratum equals the Table 2 value, for example SCP 0.630, DLS 0.660 and SDLC 0.891. Section 6.6 nevertheless writes that 'the stratum-wise coverage of every stratified method was unchanged, as Corollary 1(i) states', which reads as empirical confirmation, and RQ4 and Section 5.5 call it a 'positive control'.
issues.corrective_action: Reword Sections 5.5 and 6.6: under whole-stratum re-weighting, stratum-wise coverage is unchanged for every method by definition. The informative quantity is the marginal coverage under the shift (stratified 0.904-0.906 against marginal 0.838-0.877), which follows from the stratum-wise guarantee. Drop the claim that this verifies Corollary 1(i), or keep only the remark that it illustrates the corollary. Also state in Section 5.5 that all tilts re-weight a fixed test set, while the genuine label shift appears only in the synthetic study (Table S10).

issues.title: Conformal-selection baseline uses null-only p-value denominators, unlike its docstring and Jin & Candès
issues.evidence: The docstring of conformal_pvalues in experiments/tail_alerts.py says 'the denominator uses the whole calibration set'. The code divides by len(s_null_cal)+1, about 0.9 n, which makes every p-value about 11% larger, so BH runs at an effective level of about q/1.11. On seed 0 (31 datasets, read-only recomputation), CS-BH-0.2 mean upper-tail recall is 0.629 as coded and 0.641 with the full-calibration denominator. The effect is small but slightly weakens a baseline.
issues.corrective_action: Use (len(s_cal)+1) in the denominator, as in Jin & Candès' clipped-score p-value, or correct the docstring and state in Section 5.4 that p-values are computed against null calibration units only (valid but conservative). Re-run tail_alerts.py, which takes minutes.

issues.title: Rendering defects in reported p-values
issues.evidence:
In manuscript_filled.md:
- Line 272 (twice) and line 310: '$p\le$ < 0.001'. The template writes '$p\le$ {{...}}' and the placeholder already contains '< 0.001'.
- Line 462: 'Holm $p$ < 0.001 or smaller'.
- Table 7 (line 394): 'median difference -0.0000'.
issues.corrective_action: Fix the templates in 04_results.md lines 9, 25 and 88: drop '\le' when the value is rendered as '< 0.001', and replace 'or smaller' with 'for every comparison'. Format the C-H4 median differences so that negative zero prints as 0.0000 (for example -1.4e-5 shown as '< 0.0001 in absolute value').
